title:
Base type for all collections. Collections always have an "element type" and maps additionally have a "key type".
Collections normally may not include `null` elements, but nulls may be allowed using the "allows empty" syntax:
`[?int]` (see {@link Array}).

An {@link Array} is a 1-dimensional, ordered set of elements that allows duplicates. All values are kept in memory.

A {@link Set} is a 1-dimensional, unordered set of elements that does _not_ allow duplicates. All values are kept in
memory.

A {@link Map} is an unordered set key/value pairs. It does not allow duplicate keys, but does allow duplicate
elements. All elements are kept in memory.

A {@link Stream} is a producer of elements. The elements need not necessarily all be in memory, and whenever the
number of elements is large, streams are the preferred way to work with them to avoid memory problems.

Collections provide a rich set of functional programming methods to operate on them concisely and efficiently.
We strongly recommend using this style rather than explicit iteration.
